websearch.worst: A: omits Freedman/CCHP JWST result (H0=70.4, ~3%, overlapping Planck, tension possibly resolved); summary says only that tension is unresolved/worse
websearch.worst_summary_quote: Universe Today reports that the new results make the tension slightly worse
websearch.worst_page_quote: suggesting the tension may have been resolved after all.
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader would think JWST data uniformly show the tension persisting or worsening and that no newer study exists, missing the 2025 JWST result of 70.4 km/s/Mpc that overlaps Planck.
websearch.notes: No primary study among links; Crowded No More (arXiv 2307.15806) used for webfetch. Summary also attributes the 'worsens' claim to Universe Today but it comes from the Freethink (Ethan Siegel) page (index 9); also claims no 2025-2026 study found though the astronomynow 2025 link is in its own results.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: Summarize what this paper says about recent JWST measurements and the Hubble tension: the measured values of the Hubble constant, the uncertainties, and whether the paper concludes the tension is resolved, persists, or is unresolved. Quote the key numbers.
webfetch.notes: Spot-checked numbers (20% to 7%, 31.813, 31.792, strongest evidence quote) match the page; the '0.18 mag' tension figure was not found by simple grep, unconfirmed. First H2 run hit the wrong arXiv ID (my error) and was discarded; rerun on the correct one.
